title: The objection from God's oath in Numbers 14
source_text: XVII. Neque majorem vim habet argumentum quod petunt illi quos impugnamus, ex libri Numerorum capite 14. Ubi dicitur Deus jurasse se introducturum populum suum in terram Canaan; & tamen propter ipsorum peccatum atque incredulitatem rursus jurat se non amplius id facturum. Vivo ego, ait Dominus, sicut loquuti estis audiente me, sic faciam vobis. In solitudine hac jacebunt cadavera vestra. Omnes qui numerati estis a viginti annis & supra, & murmurastis contra me, non intrabitis terram super quam levavi manum meam, ut habitare vos facerem, praeter Caleb filium Jephune, & Josue filium Nun. Quis enim, inquiunt, ex ipsis hominibus ita amens est, ut ex animo juret se aliquid facturum, quod se facturum minime esse jam probe novit, seu causas, cur id nullo modo facturus sit, jam exploratissimas habeat? Aut quid Deo indignius, quam se aliquid facturum jurare, non animo, sed verbis tantum?
pass_a_gloss: Nor has the argument greater force which those whom we oppose seek from the 14th chapter of the book of Numbers. Where God is said to have sworn that he would bring his people into the land of Canaan; and yet on account of their sin and unbelief he swears again that he will no more do it. As I live, says the Lord, as ye have spoken in my hearing, so will I do to you. In this wilderness shall your carcasses lie. All ye that were numbered from twenty years old and upward, and have murmured against me, ye shall not enter the land concerning which I lifted up my hand, to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun. For who, they say, among men themselves is so mad, as to swear from the heart that he will do something, which he already well knows he will by no means do, or has already most thoroughly explored causes why he will in no way do it? Or what is more unworthy of God, than to swear he will do something, not in mind, but in words only?
pass_b_english: The argument our opponents draw from Numbers 14 has no more force. There God is said to have sworn that he would bring his people into the land of Canaan, and yet, because of their sin and unbelief, he swears again that he will no longer do so: 'As I live, says the Lord, I will do to you just as you have spoken in my hearing. Your corpses will lie in this wilderness. None of you who were counted, from twenty years old and upward, and who grumbled against me, will enter the land I swore with raised hand to settle you in, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.'

'For what man,' they ask, 'is so mad as to swear in earnest that he will do something he already knows full well he will not do, or for which he already has thoroughly established reasons why he will by no means do it? And what is more unworthy of God than to swear that he will do something only in words and not in intention?'

lemmas.gloss: not in mind, but in words only

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
